title: Jeremiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 6.

questions.question: Who is instructed to gather themselves and flee out of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The instruction is given to 'O ye children of Benjamin' to flee out of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 6:1.

questions.question: What has the Lord likened the daughter of Zion to?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 6:2, the Lord likens the daughter of Zion to 'a comely and delicate woman'.

questions.question: What does the Lord say will be heard continually in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 6:7, 'violence and spoil is heard in her; before me continually is grief and wounds.'

questions.question: Prepare ye war against her; arise, and let us go up at what time?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:4 states, 'Prepare ye war against her; arise, and let us go up at noon.'

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds with their flocks shall come unto Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:3 indicates that 'The shepherds with their flocks shall come unto her.'

questions.question: What did the Lord say would happen to the inhabitants of the land?
options: They will be turned into a wasteland
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:12 states, 'And their houses shall be turned unto others, with their fields and wives together.'

questions.question: True or False: The people are described as having delight in the word of the Lord.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:10 states that 'the word of the LORD is unto them a reproach; they have no delight in it.'

questions.question: What should Jerusalem be instructed to avoid, according to the Lord?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:8 warns Jerusalem to be instructed 'lest I make thee desolate, a land not inhabited.'

questions.question: Who will the Lord bring evil upon, according to Jeremiah 6:19?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:19 indicates that the Lord will bring evil upon 'this people.'

questions.question: True or False: The people were ashamed of their abominations.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:15 states, 'Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 6, what is instructed to be done against Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:6 instructs to 'Hew ye down trees, and cast a mount against Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe the people's wickedness?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:7 compares the people's wickedness to 'As a fountain casteth out her waters, so she casteth out her wickedness.'

questions.question: What does the Lord say about the remnant of Israel?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:9 states, 'They shall throughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine.'

questions.question: In which verse does the Lord command to stand in the ways and ask for the old paths?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:16 contains the command to 'Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths.'

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to the children abroad and the assembly of young men due to His fury?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will pour out His fury upon the children abroad and the assembly of young men, indicating they will be taken (Jeremiah 6:11).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 6:12, what will happen to the houses of the people?
options: They shall be turned unto others
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be turned unto others
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that their houses shall be turned unto others, indicating a loss for the current inhabitants (Jeremiah 6:12).

questions.question: What is described as the common behavior of people from the least to the greatest according to Jeremiah 6:13?
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that every one, from the least to the greatest, deals falsely, highlighting widespread dishonesty (Jeremiah 6:13).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 6:14, what false assurance do the people receive regarding their situation?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the people have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, claiming 'Peace, peace' when there is no peace (Jeremiah 6:14).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 6:15 say about the people's shame regarding their actions?
options: They were not at all ashamed
questions.correctAnswer: They were not at all ashamed
questions.explanation: The verse states that the people were not ashamed of their abominations, reflecting a lack of repentance or awareness of their sin (Jeremiah 6:15).

questions.question: What does the LORD instruct His people to seek in Jeremiah 6:16?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructs the people to ask for the old paths where the good way is, indicating a desire for them to return to righteous living (Jeremiah 6:16).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 6:17, what did the LORD set over His people?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD set watchmen over His people to warn them, indicating His desire for them to heed warnings (Jeremiah 6:17).

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Jeremiah 6:19 for the people who have rejected the LORD's words?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that because the people have not hearkened unto the LORD's words, He will bring evil upon them as a consequence (Jeremiah 6:19).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 6:20, what does the LORD say about the offerings from Sheba?
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that the burnt offerings and sacrifices from Sheba are not acceptable to the LORD, reflecting His disapproval of their worship (Jeremiah 6:20).

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 6:11, the LORD feels calm about the state of His people.
questions.explanation: The verse reveals that the LORD is full of fury, indicating He is not calm about the state of His people (Jeremiah 6:11).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 6:14 indicates that the prophets and priests were healing the hurt of the people sincerely.
questions.explanation: The verse states they healed the hurt slightly by falsely claiming peace, showing insincerity in their healing (Jeremiah 6:14).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 6:19 say will happen to the people because they rejected the LORD's law?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly indicates that the people will face evil as a result of rejecting the LORD's words and law (Jeremiah 6:19).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 6:18 urge the nations to do regarding the people of Israel?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs the nations to hear and know what is among the people of Israel, urging awareness of their situation (Jeremiah 6:18).

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 6 teach us about the importance of heeding warnings?
options: Warnings are only for the weak
questions.explanation: The text illustrates through the warnings given by watchmen that ignoring them leads to dire consequences, emphasizing the importance of heeding God's warnings (Jeremiah 6:17).

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the consequences of covetousness and deceit in leadership?
questions.explanation: The passage points to the widespread covetousness and deceit among leaders, which brings about the judgment of the people (Jeremiah 6:13).

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 6.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will lay before the people in Jeremiah 6:21?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Behold, I will lay stumblingblocks before this people...' indicating that the LORD will set obstacles in their path due to their disobedience.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 6:23, how is the approaching nation described?
questions.explanation: The verse describes the nation as 'cruel, and have no mercy' indicating their violent nature as they prepare for war.

questions.question: What emotion does Jeremiah 6:24 express regarding the news of the coming danger?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that 'anguish hath taken hold of us,' expressing deep distress due to the impending threat.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 6:26, what does the LORD tell His people to do in response to the coming destruction?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs the people to 'gird thee with sackcloth, and wallow thyself in ashes,' indicating a call for mourning and repentance.

questions.question: What is described as the state of the people in Jeremiah 6:28?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'They are all grievous revolters,' highlighting their rebellion and corruption.

questions.question: What does the term 'reprobate silver' refer to in Jeremiah 6:30?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'Reprobate silver shall men call them,' signifying that the people are deemed worthless and rejected by the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: In Jeremiah 6:10, it is said that the people delight in the word of the LORD.
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'they have no delight in it,' indicating their rejection of the LORD's word.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage reflects a similar theme of impending judgment as seen in Jeremiah 6:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 5:20 speaks of woe to those who call evil good and good evil, paralleling the concept of judgment for disobedience presented in Jeremiah 6:19.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Jeremiah 6:16 when it refers to 'the old paths'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'old paths' serves as a metaphor for traditional ways of living according to God's commands, emphasizing the importance of following them.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 6:17 indicates that the watchmen set by the LORD were heeded by the people.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But they said, We will not hearken,' indicating that the people ignored the watchmen's warnings.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 6:22, what is said to come from the north country?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Behold, a people cometh from the north country,' indicating the arrival of a powerful adversary.

questions.question: Which verse in Jeremiah 6 indicates that the inhabitants will suffer loss, including fields and wives?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And their houses shall be turned unto others, with their fields and wives together,' signifying the loss they will endure.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 6:9 imply about the remnant of Israel?
options: They will be saved without effort
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that 'They shall throughly glean the remnant of Israel as a vine,' implying a careful search and selection of what remains.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah liken the daughter of Zion to in Jeremiah 6:2?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:2 states, 'I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman,' which emphasizes her vulnerability and beauty.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 6:6, what does the LORD of hosts command regarding Jerusalem?
options: Hew down trees and cast a mount against her
questions.correctAnswer: Hew down trees and cast a mount against her
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:6 says, 'For thus hath the LORD of hosts said, Hew ye down trees, and cast a mount against Jerusalem,' indicating preparation for judgment.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'peace, peace' signify in Jeremiah 6:14?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:14 states, 'They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace,' which indicates a false sense of security.

questions.question: What does God say about the people's response to His word in Jeremiah 6:10?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 6:10, it is stated, 'behold, their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken,' showing their inability to listen to God's warnings.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Jeremiah 6:15 for those who are not ashamed of their abominations?
options: They shall fall among them that fall
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall among them that fall
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:15 says, 'therefore they shall fall among them that fall,' indicating judgment for their lack of shame over sin.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 6:19 reveal about the consequences of rejecting God's law?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:19 states, 'behold, I will bring evil upon this people...because they have not hearkened unto my words,' indicating dire consequences for disobedience.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do in Jeremiah 6:21 regarding the people?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 6:21, the LORD declares, 'Behold, I will lay stumblingblocks before this people,' indicating judgment and obstacles due to their sinful choices.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 6:22, where does the great nation come from that the LORD speaks of?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:22 states, 'Behold, a people cometh from the north country,' referring to the invading nation as a form of judgment from God.

questions.question: What emotional state does Jeremiah describe in Jeremiah 6:24 in response to the impending danger?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:24 expresses, 'anguish hath taken hold of us, and pain, as of a woman in travail,' highlighting the deep distress felt by the people.

questions.question: What warning does the LORD give in Jeremiah 6:27 regarding Jeremiah's role?
options: To be a tower and fortress
questions.correctAnswer: To be a tower and fortress
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 6:27, the LORD says, 'I have set thee for a tower and a fortress among my people,' indicating Jeremiah's role in safeguarding and guiding them.

questions.question: What overarching theme does Jeremiah 6:16 convey about the people's choices?
options: Choosing the old paths leads to rest
New paths are better than old ones
God has no preference for direction
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing the old paths leads to rest
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:16 emphasizes, 'Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths...and ye shall find rest for your souls,' underscoring the importance of following God's ways.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 6:28 describe the state of the people?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:28 states, 'They are all grievous revolters, walking with slanders,' depicting the people's rebellion and corruption.

questions.question: What does the LORD express in Jeremiah 6:11 about His feelings towards the people?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 6:11, the LORD says, 'I am full of the fury of the LORD,' indicating His intense anger towards the unfaithful people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not judge sin. What does Jeremiah 6:19 actually teach?
options: God brings evil upon His people
God is indifferent to our actions
questions.correctAnswer: God brings evil upon His people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 6:19 states, 'I will bring evil upon this people...because they have not hearkened unto my words,' affirming God's active judgment against sin.

questions.question: What message does Jeremiah convey about the future of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 6:8?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 6:8, it is warned, 'lest I make thee desolate, a land not inhabited,' indicating the severe consequences of unrepentance.
